I am Dr. Agent. I see you have no prior dialogue and no specific symptoms listed in your initial input. To begin our assessment of your dermatological condition, please describe the appearance, location, and any changes in the skin lesions you are concerned about.

REQUEST TEST: Physical_Examination_Focus (Lesion Morphology and Distribution)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Inspection reveals an erythematous plaque with areas of crusting, oozing, and irregular borders observed on the dorsal surface of the penile shaft and on the left middle finger. Palpation shows lesions are firm to touch, non-tender, with no warmth. Regional lymph nodes are clear with no palpable cervical, axillary, or inguinal lymphadenopathy. Biopsy findings indicate cells with nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within the follicle-bearing epithelium. STD Panel results are negative for Syphilis, HIV, HBV, and HCV.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma

The biopsy results showing nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures, combined with the clinical presentation of a firm, crusted plaque with irregular borders on the penile shaft and finger, are highly characteristic of Squamous Cell Carcinoma. The negative STD panel and lack of lymphadenopathy help rule out infectious etiologies and early metastatic spread, pointing toward a primary cutaneous malignancy.
